title: Finite rational-point interpolation by a smooth curve in an integral variety
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme], separated and of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $F\subseteq X(k)$ be a finite nonempty set of $k$-rational points [def-pc-rational-point]. There exist a smooth separated connected finite-type $k$-scheme $D$ of dimension exactly one [def-sc-curves, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], a $k$-morphism $g:D\to X$, and points $d_s\in D(k)$ for $s\in F$, with $g\circ d_s=s$ for every $s\in F$. Here connected means that the underlying space is nonempty and is not a disjoint union of two nonempty open subsets. No positive-dimensional, smoothness, properness, or quasi-projectivity hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 1.9 (printed p.4), y=1, followed by normalization of the reduced integral curve. Supporting Stacks Tags 0BXR (varieties.tex lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic), 0BX2 (properties.tex lemma-normal-dimension-1-regular), and 038X (varieties.tex lemma-geometrically-regular-smooth); over perfect k geometric regularity equals regularity because there are no nontrivial finite purely inseparable extensions. The zero-dimensional case is the constant map from the projective line. This is an agent-assembled consequence, not the verbatim assertion of Corollary 1.9.

proof.text: By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] and the nonemptiness in [def-pc-integral-scheme], $m=\dim X$ is a nonnegative integer. Each section $s:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion], since $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated. Thus the images of $F$ are a finite nonempty set of closed points.

source.place: Tag 01KT, lemma-section-immersion; dimension finiteness as in lem-kun-dimension-finite-type

proof.text: If $m=0$, irreducibility and the definition of dimension imply that $|X|$ has one point: another point would have a proper nonempty irreducible closure, giving a chain of length one. Any affine neighbourhood is therefore all of $X$, say $X=\operatorname{Spec}L$. The domain $L$ has only the prime $(0)$, hence is a field. A chosen $s_0\in F$ gives a $k$-algebra map $L\to k$ splitting $k\to L$; injectivity and the fact its image contains $k$ make it an isomorphism. Hence $X\simeq\operatorname{Spec}k$ and all the sections in $F$ agree. Take $D=\mathbf P^1_k$, a smooth proper connected curve by [lem-asd-projective-line-genus-zero], take $g$ constant with value $s_0$, and use $[1:0]$ for every $d_s$. Properness includes separatedness and finite type, so this gives the required zero-dimensional case.

source.place: Tag 0B2P, lemma-projective-space-smooth, n=1; elementary zero-dimensional reduction

proof.text: Assume $m\geq1$. We construct integral separated finite-type closed subschemes $C_r\subseteq X$ containing the same closed points, with $\dim C_r=r$, by descending induction on $r$ from $m$ to $1$. Start with $C_m=X$. For $r\geq2$, apply [lem-sfb-bertini-prescribed-point-dimension-cut] to $C_r$ and the marked points, closed also in $C_r$, to obtain $C_{r-1}\hookrightarrow C_r$. Composing the inclusions gives the required closed immersion into $X$: on affine opens the ring maps are successive surjections. Thus $C=C_1$ is integral, separated, finite type, of dimension one, and contains every marked point. A section $s$ factors through $C$ since the defining ideal lies in the kernel of evaluation at its image (the residue-field point is exactly the given $k$-point). Denote this factorization by $c_s$. For $m=1$ this construction simply takes $C=X$.

source.place: Theorem 1.8 iterated, equivalently the proof of Corollary 1.9, printed p.4

proof.text:
Let $
u:D=C^
u	o C$ be [def-sc-normalization]. By [lem-sc-normalization-exists], $
u$ is finite and surjective and $\dim D=\dim C=1$. Its affine charts are integral closures of domains inside the common function field, hence are domains with a common generic point; consequently $D$ is integral and nonempty, and thus connected. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-separated-finite-type], $D$ is separated and of finite type over $k$. An algebraically closed field is perfect: it has no nontrivial algebraic field extensions. Apply [lem-sc-normalized-curve-smooth] to conclude that $D$ is smooth over $k$.

source.place: Tag 0BXR, lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic; Tag 038X, lemma-geometrically-regular-smooth; normal dimension-one regularity is properties.tex Tag 0BX2

proof.text:
For each $s\in F$, choose an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $c_s$ in $C$. Write $
u^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ finite over $A$, using [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The fibre at $c_s$ has ring $B\otimes_A k$, a finite-dimensional $k$-algebra; it is nonzero because $
u$ is surjective. A maximal ideal of this algebra gives a field quotient finite-dimensional over $k$, hence equal to $k$ since $k$ is algebraically closed. The resulting $k$-algebra map $B\otimes_A k	o k$ gives $d_s\in D(k)$ with $
u d_s=c_s$. This argument works even when $c_s$ is singular or has several branches; only one branch is chosen.

source.place: Tag 01WH, definition-integral-finite; elementary finite-algebra quotient argument over an algebraically closed field

proof.text: Let $i:C\hookrightarrow X$ be the constructed inclusion and set $g=i\circ\nu$. For every $s\in F$, $g\circ d_s=i\circ\nu\circ d_s=i\circ c_s=s$. The preceding steps give every required property of $D$.

I checked Charles–Poonen printed pp.3–4. Their varieties are separated and of finite type. Theorem 1.8: a geometrically irreducible X of dim m≥2 and finite closed F give Y⊆X of dim m−1 containing F. The proof (Nagata and Chow reductions, Y=H_f∩X̄′, proper image, then restriction to the open X) makes Y closed, so the 'closed immersion' in the new node is justified. Over k=k̄ an integral X is geometrically irreducible, and the reduced Y is integral, separated and of finite type. Empty F is allowed as in the source. New node lem-sfb-bertini-prescribed-point-dimension-cut: statement only and self-contained, with all notions cited. blueprint_refs ancestor gives None and the Bertini search finds 0 blueprint nodes, so same_as=[] is right. It has 4 search kinds. It is not a restatement: it is a codimension-one cut, while the item does the induction, the dim-0 case, normalization and the lifts. rg over the DAG finds only smooth-affine or F̄_q Bertini nodes (lem-zl-bertini-*, sk-lem-wgen-bertini-cover), so there is no duplicate. Item statement (unchanged except TeX) tested on X=Spec k (P^1, constant map), the nodal cubic through its node, and a singular surface. Steps: (1) dimension finite and ≥0; sections are closed immersions by the separated-section leaf. (2) m=0: one point, X=Spec L with L a field, the section gives L≅k; lem-asd-projective-line-genus-zero gives P^1 as a connected curve (def-sc-curves) and properness gives separated and finite type. (3) descending induction is set up properly (claim, base C_m=X, transition for r≥2 by the new node, whose hypotheses hold in C_r); closed immersions compose; s factors through C because O_{X,x}→k kills I_x⊆m_x. (4) def-sc-normalization for integral C; lem-sc-normalization-exists gives finite, surjective, dim 1; D is integral because all generic points lie over η with fibre Spec K, so D is connected; lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-separated-finite-type gives separated and finite type; lem-sc-normalized-curve-smooth applies (k̄ perfect). Both normalization nodes are slopmaster2-closed, so the off-unit use is accepted. (5) the fibre B⊗_A k is finite and nonzero by surjectivity, and a maximal quotient is k, giving d_s; this is elementary. (6) composition gives g∘d_s=s. Accepted tool_uses: lem-kun-dimension-finite-type, lem-asd-projective-line-genus-zero (only the clause that P^1 is a smooth proper connected curve), lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-separated-finite-type. Nit: step 3 could also list def-weil-closed-immersion. No SGA is cited and no fixes were written.
